notes:
Account came inbound after public benchmark report (EU region numbers). They forwarded the interactive table internally and asked if we can hold p95 steady under load and how Dedicated/Private maps to their residency requirements.

High-level: payments platform w/ strong EU footprint (merchant + consumer). They are exploring LLM for internal ops + customer support (summarize disputes, chargeback evidence, KYC/AML case notes) and eventually an agent-assisted workflow for risk analysts.

What resonated:
- EU region performance in the benchmark (their comment: "finally someone publishing p95 + cost in the same chart")
- Consistency story (same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private; ability to start Hosted for pilot then move into VPC)

Key requirements (from discovery + follow-up email):
- Latency SLO: target p95 <= 700ms end-to-end for short prompts ("support macro suggestions") and p95 <= 1.8s for medium context summarization requests in EU. They care more about p95 stability than best-case p50.
- Throughput: initial pilot ~30 RPS peak EU business hours, growth to 100+ RPS if rolled out to all support queues.
- Workload mix: mostly chat-style generation + summarization; some embeddings for internal doc search (policy + dispute templates).
- Reliability: wants clear fallback behavior (region fallback *within EU only*) and explicit capacity guarantees.
- Compliance/security: SOC 2 Type II is table stakes; they also asked about audit logs, retention controls, and KMS integration. SSO/SAML required for Console access.
- Data residency: strong preference for EU-only processing and EU-only log storage for the inference service; avoid any US-based processing for prompt/response content. (They may allow US for billing metadata; need to confirm.)

Products discussed:
- Dedicated: primary path for predictable throughput + isolation. They want a sizing proposal for an EU region footprint.
- Private/VPC: procurement/security team leaning this direction for production if we can keep ops burden low. They asked if the control plane can be private and whether audit logs can be exported.
- Optimize: they liked the idea of cost/quality guardrails, but it’s secondary to security + latency.

Procurement / timeline:
- They’re aiming to shortlist vendors by early Aug, security review in Aug, and have a pilot SOW signed by late Aug. Production decision targeted Sept (aligned to Q4 roadmap). They mentioned a “hard stop” procurement freeze late Sept.
